topics.title: Hide and seek: who can see what?

learn.hook: In hide and seek, the best hiding spot is one the seeker cannot see. Where would you hide?
points: Position words tell where things are: behind, in front of, beside, above, below, between, under.
From where you stand, things hidden behind a wall, a tree or a big object cannot be seen.
If you move to a new spot, you may see things that were hidden before.
From high above, like from a rooftop or a tree, you can see things that are hidden from the ground.

example.q: Raju hides behind a big water tank. Meera stands in front of the tank. Can Meera see Raju?
steps: The tank is between Meera and Raju.

learn.reallife: When you play hide and seek at a wedding or in a park, you choose spots behind pillars, cars or bushes so the seeker cannot see you.

items.text: The cat is ___ the table, so it is closer to the floor than the table top.
Asha sits ___ Ravi and Gita, in the middle.
The bat is lying ___ the ball, side by side.

games.title: Can it be seen?
items: Someone behind a closed door can be seen from outside.
The door blocks the view.
From a rooftop you can see children hiding behind a wall in the yard.
Looking from above, the wall does not block the view.
If a tree is between you and a friend, the tree may hide your friend.
Things in between can block the view.
A person standing in front of you is hidden from you.
Nothing blocks them, so you can see them.
Moving to another spot can show you something that was hidden.
From a new place, the thing blocking your view may no longer be in the way.

quiz.q: A ball is under a chair. Which sentence is correct?
options: The ball is on the chair
The chair is under the ball
The ball is below the seat of the chair
The ball is above the chair
quiz.explain: Under the chair means the ball is below the seat.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up above and below

quiz.q: Sonu stands in front of a big truck. Tina is hiding behind the truck. Can Sonu see Tina?
quiz.explain: The truck is between them, so it hides Tina from Sonu.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that things in between block the view

quiz.q: Where can the seeker go to see children hiding behind the bushes in a park?
options: Up on a high slide looking down
quiz.explain: From high above, you can see over the bushes.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that height helps to see hidden things

quiz.q: Gita is between Ali and Bina in a line. Who is in the middle?
quiz.explain: Between two people means in the middle of them.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'between'

quiz.q: A cat sits on top of a cupboard. A dog sleeps on the floor in front of the cupboard. Which is true?
options: The dog is on the cupboard
The dog is above the cat
The cat is above the dog
The cat is under the cupboard
quiz.explain: The cat is on top of the cupboard, high up, so it is above the dog.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up above and below

quiz.q: Mohit hides behind a pillar. The seeker walks round to the other side of the pillar. What happens?
options: The seeker can now see Mohit
quiz.explain: From the other side, the pillar is no longer between them.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a hidden thing stays hidden from every spot

quiz.q: From a drone high above a playground, which of these can be seen?
options: Children behind a wall, and the tops of everything
quiz.explain: From directly above, walls do not hide the ground behind them.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a view from above shows less

quiz.q: Four children hide: one under a table, one behind a door, one beside a sofa, one in front of a window. Who can the seeker standing at the window easily see?
options: The one in front of the window
quiz.explain: The child in front of the window is right near the seeker with nothing blocking the view.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about what blocks the view

teach.ask: Gappu is playing hide and seek. Explain to Gappu how to choose a good hiding spot.
teach.praise: I will hide behind the tank so it blocks the view, but not where someone up high can see me!
teach.nudge: What makes something hidden, and can someone from above still see you?

learn.hook: A bird on a tree and an ant on the ground look at the same bucket. Do they see the same shape?
points: The same object can look different from the top, the front and the side.
The top view is what you see from straight above, like a bird.
The front view is what you see when you stand in front of it.
From one side you see only that side. Things on the other side stay hidden.
A ball looks like a circle from every direction. A dice looks like a square from every direction.

example.q: Riya stacks 3 cubes one on top of the other to make a tower. What does she see from the top and from the front?
steps: From straight above, only the top cube's face shows: 1 square.
From the front, all 3 cubes show, one above the other: 3 squares in a column.
example.answer: Top: 1 square. Front: 3 squares in a column.

learn.reallife: Maps and drone photos show places from the top. A photo of your house from the road shows its front view.

games.title: Match the view to the shape
pairs: A standing glass from the front
A party cap from the front

games.title: True or false?
items: From the top, a cone standing on its base looks like a circle.
Looking down, you see its round base with the tip in the middle.
A dice looks like a circle from the top.
Every face of a dice is a square, so the top view is a square.
From one side of a car, you can see all 4 of its wheels.
From one side you see only the 2 wheels on that side.
Top view means looking from straight above.
Like a bird looking down from the sky.
The front view and the top view of a cube are both squares.
All faces of a cube are squares, so every view is a square.
A ball looks like a triangle from the side.
A ball is a sphere, which looks like a circle from every side.

quiz.q: From straight above, what shape does a bucket standing upright look like?
quiz.explain: Looking down into a bucket you see its round rim, which is a circle.
quiz.mistake: Gives the side view of the bucket

quiz.q: Arjun stands in front of a tall water tank shaped like a cylinder. What shape does he see?
quiz.explain: From the front, a standing cylinder has a straight side, a flat top and a flat bottom, so it looks like a rectangle.
quiz.mistake: Gives the top view (circle) instead of the front view

quiz.q: Aisha looks at a car from one side. How many wheels can she see?
quiz.explain: A car has 2 wheels on each side. From one side the other 2 wheels are hidden.
quiz.mistake: Counts all the wheels the car has, not the ones she can see

quiz.q: Kabir stacks 4 cubes one on top of the other. Looking from straight above, how many cube faces can he see?
quiz.explain: From the top he sees only the top face of the highest cube. The others are hidden below it.
quiz.mistake: Counts all the cubes in the tower

quiz.q: Kabir looks at the same tower of 4 cubes from the front. How many squares does he see?
quiz.explain: From the front, every cube in the tower shows one face. So he sees 4 squares, one above the other.
quiz.mistake: Gives the top view answer

quiz.q: A bird flying over a house sees its roof. What do we call this view?
quiz.explain: Looking from straight above is called the top view.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names of the views

quiz.q: Which object looks like a circle from the top AND a rectangle from the front?
quiz.explain: A glass is a cylinder: round from the top, rectangle from the front. A ball is a circle both ways, a dice is a square, and a cap is a triangle from the front.
quiz.mistake: Checks only one of the two views

quiz.q: Meena holds a round steel plate flat and looks at it exactly from the side, at eye level. What does she see?
quiz.explain: A plate is very thin. From the side you see only its thin edge, like a flat strip.
quiz.mistake: Gives the top view of the plate

teach.ask: Gappu saw a glass from the top and from the front and got two different shapes! How can one glass look like two shapes?
teach.praise: Now I see! Where you look from changes the shape you see. Thank you!
teach.nudge: Does it matter where Gappu is looking from? Tell me about top and front.

topics.title: Views of a brick and drawing views

learn.hook: Three friends look at the same brick and draw three different rectangles. Who is right? All of them!
points: A brick is a cuboid. From the top, the front and the side, you see three different rectangles.
The one looking from straight above sees the top view. The one in front sees the front view. The one at the end sees the side view.
To draw a view, imagine looking straight at the object from that side and draw only the outline you see.
A pencil lying down looks like a long thin rectangle from the top, but like a small hexagon or circle from its end.

example.q: A brick lies flat on the ground. Anu looks from the top, Babu from the long front side, Chotu from the short end. Who sees the smallest rectangle?
steps: The top is long and wide: biggest rectangle.
The front is long but thin.
The end is short and thin: smallest.
So Chotu sees the smallest rectangle.

learn.reallife: Architects draw a top view (plan), a front view and a side view of a house before builders begin work.

games.title: Match the view
pairs: Tall rectangle with a narrow neck
A brick from its short end

games.title: Which view is it?
items: Looking down from the ceiling
Standing in front of the cupboard
A bird looking at a roof
Looking at a car door from the road
Seeing a chair's seat from above
Seeing a chair from its side

quiz.q: A brick lies flat on a table. Which child sees its biggest rectangle?
options: The one looking from the top
The one at its short end
quiz.explain: A flat brick shows its biggest face on top, the long and wide face.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all views of a brick are the same

quiz.q: What shape is the top view of a water bottle standing on a table?
quiz.explain: Looking down on a round bottle, you see a circle.
quiz.mistake: Draws the front view instead

quiz.q: A six-sided pencil lies on the table. What do you see from its sharpened end, looking straight at the tip?
options: A small hexagon with a point in the middle
quiz.explain: From the end, you look at the six-sided pencil, so you see a hexagon with the tip in the middle.
quiz.mistake: Draws the long side instead of the end view

quiz.q: A cap with a round top and a front peak is seen from the top. What do you see?
options: A circle with the peak sticking out
quiz.explain: From above you see the round crown and the peak sticking out in front.
quiz.mistake: Does not imagine looking down

quiz.q: Which view of a chair shows its back as a tall shape and its seat as a thin line?
quiz.explain: From the side, the back stands up tall and the seat looks like a thin line.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up side view and top view

quiz.q: Three children see a brick and draw: a big rectangle, a long thin rectangle, a small rectangle. How many different views did they draw?
quiz.explain: Top, front and side views are three different rectangles.
quiz.mistake: Thinks they are all the same view

quiz.q: Which object looks like a circle from the top and a rectangle from the side?
quiz.explain: A standing tin can (cylinder) is round from the top and a rectangle from the side.
quiz.mistake: Picks a ball, which is a circle from every side

quiz.q: To draw the front view of a cupboard, where should you imagine standing?
quiz.explain: The front view is what you see when you face the object from the front.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up front view and top view

teach.ask: Gappu drew a brick from the top but called it the side view. How can Gappu tell which view is which?
teach.praise: Top is from above, front is from in front, side is from the end. I see it now!
teach.nudge: Where do you stand to see each view?

topics.title: Spatial thinking: blocks, places and directions

learn.hook: Can you count blocks you cannot even see? Let's play hide and seek with cubes!
points: In a stack, some blocks hide behind or under others. Count row by row and layer by layer.
A wall that is 4 cubes long and 2 cubes high has 4 + 4 = 8 cubes.
Left and right change when you turn around. Things that were on your right are now on your left.
On most maps North is at the top, South at the bottom, East on the right and West on the left.
Position words like in front, behind, above, below, left and right help us find things.

example.q: Arjun builds steps: 3 cubes in the bottom row, 2 in the middle row and 1 on top. How many cubes did he use?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers stack boxes in layers. Auto drivers use left, right and map directions to find your house.

items.text: If you turn around, things on your right are now on your ___.
On a map with North at the top, South is at the ___.
On a map with North at the top, East is on the ___.
Steps made of 2 cubes with 1 cube on top use ___ cubes.

quiz.q: A wall of cubes is 5 cubes long and 2 cubes high. How many cubes are in the wall?
quiz.explain: Each row has 5 cubes and there are 2 rows. 5 + 5 = 10.
quiz.mistake: Adds the length and height instead of counting every row

quiz.q: Steps are built with 4 cubes at the bottom, then 3, then 2, then 1 on top. How many cubes in all?
quiz.explain: Add every row: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the single cube on top

quiz.q: Riya faces the school gate and the library is on her right. She turns around to face the other way. Where is the library now?
quiz.explain: When you turn around, left and right swap. So the library is now on her left.
quiz.mistake: Thinks left and right stay the same after turning around

quiz.q: Joseph builds a block with 2 layers. Each layer has 2 rows of 2 cubes. How many cubes did he use?
quiz.explain: One layer has 2 × 2 = 4 cubes. Two layers have 4 + 4 = 8 cubes, even though some are hidden inside.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the cubes that can be seen

quiz.q: 7 children stand in a row. Meena is 3rd from the left. What is her place counting from the right?
quiz.explain: There are 2 children to her left, so there are 7 - 3 = 4 children to her right. She comes next, so she is 5th from the right.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 7 - 3 and forgets to count Meena herself

quiz.q: On a map, North is at the top. Which direction is on the right side of the map?
quiz.explain: With North at the top, East is on the right, West on the left and South at the bottom.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up East and West

quiz.q: Harpreet looks in a mirror and raises her right hand. If the girl in the mirror were a real girl facing Harpreet, which of her hands would be up?
quiz.explain: A mirror flips left and right. The girl in the mirror faces Harpreet, so the raised hand is her left hand.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a mirror image is exactly the same as the real person

quiz.q: Kabir walks 4 steps forward and then 4 steps back. How many steps away from the start is he?
quiz.explain: Going 4 steps back undoes the 4 steps forward. He is back at the start, 0 steps away.
quiz.mistake: Adds the steps instead of seeing they cancel out

teach.ask: Gappu built a big block of cubes, but some cubes are hidden inside. How can Gappu count them all?
teach.praise: Brilliant! Count each layer and add them up, hidden cubes too. Gappu counted all of them!
teach.nudge: What about the cubes Gappu cannot see? How can we count those?

learn.hook: The cat is looking for Jagat in class. 'Third desk, second row!' says the teacher. Can you find him?
points: When desks are arranged in rows and columns, they form a grid.
We can say where something is by giving its row number and its desk (column) number.
Always agree where counting starts: for example, row 1 at the front and desk 1 on the left.
To find a spot, first go to the row, then count the desks along it.
Two different positions never point to the same desk; each place has its own row and desk number.

example.q: In a class grid, row 1 is at the front and desks are counted from the left. Jagat sits in row 2, desk 3. How do you find him?
steps: Jagat is at the third desk of the second row.

learn.reallife: Cinema seats are marked like 'Row F, seat 12'. Your ticket tells you the row and the seat, just like a grid!

items.text: Grid: Row 1 🐱🍎⚽ / Row 2 🌸🐶📘 / Row 3 🚗⭐🥭. 🐶 is in row ___, column 2.
Grid: Row 1 🐱🍎⚽ / Row 2 🌸🐶📘 / Row 3 🚗⭐🥭. The 🥭 is in row 3, column ___.
Grid: Row 1 🐱🍎⚽ / Row 2 🌸🐶📘 / Row 3 🚗⭐🥭. Row 1, column 3 has the ___.
Grid: Row 1 🐱🍎⚽ / Row 2 🌸🐶📘 / Row 3 🚗⭐🥭. Row 3, column 1 has the ___.

games.title: Grid facts
items: Rows and columns of desks make a grid.
Rows go across and columns go from front to back.
'Row 2, desk 3' and 'row 3, desk 2' are always the same desk.
Changing the order changes the place.
We must agree where to start counting rows and desks.
Otherwise two people may point to different desks.
A grid with 4 rows and 5 desks in each row has 20 desks.
Each desk has its own row and desk number.
No two desks share both numbers.

quiz.q: Grid (row 1 at the top): Row 1: 🐱 🍎 ⚽ | Row 2: 🌸 🐶 📘 | Row 3: 🚗 ⭐ 🥭. Columns are counted from the left. What is in row 2, column 2?
quiz.explain: Go to row 2 (🌸 🐶 📘) and count 2 from the left: 🐶.
quiz.mistake: Counts columns from the right

quiz.q: Grid (row 1 at the top): Row 1: 🐱 🍎 ⚽ | Row 2: 🌸 🐶 📘 | Row 3: 🚗 ⭐ 🥭. Columns are counted from the left. Where is the ⭐?
quiz.explain: ⭐ is in row 3, and it is the second from the left.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the row and column numbers

quiz.q: Grid (row 1 at the top): Row 1: 🐱 🍎 ⚽ | Row 2: 🌸 🐶 📘 | Row 3: 🚗 ⭐ 🥭. Columns are counted from the left. What is in row 1, column 1?
quiz.explain: Row 1 is the top row and column 1 is the first from the left: 🐱.
quiz.mistake: Starts counting from the bottom row

quiz.q: A class has 5 rows with 6 desks in each row. How many desks are there?
quiz.explain: 5 rows of 6 desks: 5 × 6 = 30.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Row 1 is at the front. Desks are counted from the left. Simran sits in row 4, desk 1. Where is she?
options: Fourth row, last desk on the right
Fourth row, first desk on the left
quiz.explain: Row 4 means the fourth row from the front. Desk 1 is the first on the left.
quiz.mistake: Swaps row and desk

quiz.q: Grid (row 1 at the top): Row 1: 🐱 🍎 ⚽ | Row 2: 🌸 🐶 📘 | Row 3: 🚗 ⭐ 🥭. Columns are counted from the left. Which choice correctly describes where the 📘 is?
quiz.explain: 📘 is in row 2, third from the left.
quiz.mistake: Reads the column as the row

quiz.q: Peter draws a 3 by 3 grid and must put a 🏏 at row 3, column 1 (row 1 at the top). Where should he draw it?
quiz.explain: Row 3 is the bottom row, and column 1 is on the left: the bottom-left box.
quiz.mistake: Counts rows from the bottom

quiz.q: Grid (row 1 at the top): Row 1: 🐱 🍎 ⚽ | Row 2: 🌸 🐶 📘 | Row 3: 🚗 ⭐ 🥭. Columns are counted from the left. How many things are in column 3?
quiz.explain: Column 3 has ⚽, 📘 and 🥭: 3 things, one in each row.
quiz.mistake: Counts a row instead of a column

teach.ask: Gappu cannot find his friend in the class. Explain how to use rows and desks to find any seat.
teach.praise: Go to the row, then count the desks! I found my friend at row 3, desk 2!
teach.nudge: Which do you find first, the row or the desk, and where do you start counting?

topics.title: Grid game: placing things with clues

learn.hook: Clue 1: the parrot is in the top-right corner. Clue 2: the mango is just below it. Can you place them all?
points: Corner words help on a grid: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right.
'Second row, second column' tells the exact box to use.
Some clues compare: 'just below', 'just to the left of', 'in the same row as'.
To solve a puzzle, place the sure things first, then use them to place the rest.

example.q: On a 3 by 3 grid, the 🦜 is in the top-right corner. The 🥭 is just below the 🦜. Where is the 🥭?
steps: Just below means one row down, same column.
So the 🥭 is in row 2, column 3.

learn.reallife: Seating plans for a class photo or a school function often use clues like 'tallest in the back row, in the middle'.

games.title: Grid words on a 3 by 3 grid (row 1 at top)
Check the clue
items: On a 3 by 3 grid, the box just below the centre is row 3, column 2.
One row down from row 2, column 2.
The top-left corner is in row 3.
Top means row 1.
A 3 by 3 grid has 9 boxes.
3 rows × 3 columns = 9.
Just to the right of row 1, column 1 is row 2, column 1.
Right keeps the same row: row 1, column 2.
Two things in the same row are side by side.
A row goes across.

quiz.q: On a 3 by 3 grid with row 1 at the top, where is the bottom-right corner?
quiz.explain: Bottom means row 3 and right means column 3.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up left and right

quiz.q: Place a 🌙 in the second row, second column of a 3 by 3 grid. Which box is that?
quiz.explain: Row 2, column 2 is right in the middle of a 3 by 3 grid.
quiz.mistake: Counts from the wrong corner

quiz.q: Clues: 🐘 is in the top-left corner. 🐯 is just to the right of 🐘. Where is 🐯 (row 1 at top)?
quiz.explain: Top-left is row 1, column 1. One to the right is row 1, column 2.
quiz.mistake: Moves down instead of right

quiz.q: Clues: ⭐ is in the centre of a 3 by 3 grid. 🌸 is just above ⭐. Where is 🌸?
quiz.explain: Centre is row 2, column 2. Just above is one row up: row 1, column 2.
quiz.mistake: Moves down instead of up

quiz.q: Clues: the 🍌 is in the bottom row. It is in the same column as the top-right corner. Where is the 🍌?
quiz.explain: Top-right corner is in column 3. Bottom row is row 3. So row 3, column 3.
quiz.mistake: Uses only one of the two clues

quiz.q: A 4 by 4 grid has 4 rows and 4 columns. How many boxes does it have?
quiz.explain: 4 rows of 4 boxes: 4 × 4 = 16.
quiz.mistake: Adds rows and columns

quiz.q: Clues on a 3 by 3 grid: 🍎 and 🍇 are in the top row. 🍎 is in a corner on the left. 🍇 is in the middle of the row. Which box of the top row is empty?
quiz.explain: 🍎 is in column 1 and 🍇 is in column 2, so column 3 is empty.
quiz.mistake: Does not combine the clues

quiz.q: Clues: 🚲 is in row 2. 🚲 is in the column just left of the centre column of a 3 by 3 grid. Where is 🚲?
quiz.explain: The centre column is column 2. Just left of it is column 1. So row 2, column 1.
quiz.mistake: Moves right instead of left

teach.ask: Gappu has 3 clues for a grid puzzle but does not know where to start. How should Gappu solve it?
teach.praise: First place the sure ones, then use them for the others. Puzzle solved!
teach.nudge: Which clue would you use first, and how do 'row' and 'column' help?

topics.title: Treasure hunt: moving on a grid

learn.hook: 2 steps right, 3 steps up... and you find the treasure chest! Can you follow the moves?
points: On a grid, a move is written as a number of steps and a direction: right, left, up or down.
Follow the moves one by one, in the order they are given.
Right and left keep you in the same row. Up and down keep you in the same column.
To give moves to a friend, count the steps across first, then up or down.
If you know where someone started and how they moved, you can tell where they ended.

example.q: Start at the bottom-left box of a grid. Move 3 steps right, then 2 steps up. How far are you from the start in all?

learn.reallife: Delivery riders follow moves like 'go 2 lanes right, then 3 houses up' to reach your home.

games.title: Moves on a grid
items: Moving right keeps you in the same row.
Right goes across the row.
Moving up keeps you in the same row.
Up keeps you in the same column.
3 right then 3 left brings you back to the start.
The moves cancel each other.
2 up then 1 down leaves you 1 step above the start.
2 − 1 = 1 step up.
Order of moves never matters on a grid with walls.
Walls or blocked boxes can make one order impossible.

quiz.q: Start at row 3, column 1 of a 3 by 3 grid (row 1 at top). Move 2 steps right. Where are you?
quiz.explain: Right keeps the row the same. Column 1 + 2 = column 3.
quiz.mistake: Moves up instead of right

quiz.q: Start at row 3, column 1. Move 2 steps up (row 1 at top). Where are you?
quiz.explain: Up takes you towards row 1: row 3 → row 2 → row 1. Column stays 1.
quiz.mistake: Adds to the row number when moving up

quiz.q: Grid (row 1 at the top): Row 1: 🐱 🍎 ⚽ | Row 2: 🌸 🐶 📘 | Row 3: 🚗 ⭐ 🥭. Columns are counted from the left. Start at 🚗. Move 1 step right, then 1 step up. Where are you?
quiz.explain: 🚗 → 1 right is ⭐ → 1 up is 🐶.
quiz.mistake: Does the moves in the wrong direction

quiz.q: Grid (row 1 at the top): Row 1: 🐱 🍎 ⚽ | Row 2: 🌸 🐶 📘 | Row 3: 🚗 ⭐ 🥭. Columns are counted from the left. Start at 🐱. Move 2 steps right, then 2 steps down. Which thing do you reach?
quiz.explain: 🐱 → 2 right is ⚽ → 2 down is 🥭.
quiz.mistake: Stops after the first move

quiz.q: Grid (row 1 at the top): Row 1: 🐱 🍎 ⚽ | Row 2: 🌸 🐶 📘 | Row 3: 🚗 ⭐ 🥭. Columns are counted from the left. Ravi starts at 🌸 and tells Sita how to reach 📘. Which moves are correct?
quiz.explain: 🌸 and 📘 are in the same row. 📘 is 2 columns to the right.
quiz.mistake: Uses up or down for things in the same row

quiz.q: Grid (row 1 at the top): Row 1: 🐱 🍎 ⚽ | Row 2: 🌸 🐶 📘 | Row 3: 🚗 ⭐ 🥭. Columns are counted from the left. Mini started at 🍎 and moved 1 down, then 1 right. What was her target?
quiz.explain: 🍎 → 1 down is 🐶 → 1 right is 📘.
quiz.mistake: Reverses the order of moves

quiz.q: Ali moves 4 steps right, 3 steps up and 1 step left on a grid. How many steps does he walk in all?
quiz.explain: 4 + 3 + 1 = 8 steps walked.
quiz.mistake: Takes away the left step

quiz.q: From the start, Neha moves 5 steps right and then 2 steps left. How many columns to the right of the start is she now?
quiz.explain: 5 right then 2 left leaves her 5 − 2 = 3 columns to the right.
quiz.mistake: Adds the left steps

teach.ask: Gappu is on a treasure map. Explain how to follow moves like '3 right, 2 up'.
teach.praise: I counted 3 boxes right, then 2 up, and found the treasure!
teach.nudge: Do you do the moves in order, and which way is right or up?

topics.title: Counting steps: which path is shorter?

learn.hook: Two paths lead to the canteen. One zigzags, one goes straight. Which saves your legs?
points: Count the steps along a path to find its length.
Different paths to the same place can have different numbers of steps.
On a grid, a path that never goes backwards takes (steps across) + (steps up or down).
A path with detours or backward steps is longer.
To find which place is nearer, count the steps to each and compare.

example.q: From the gate, the library is 3 steps right and 4 steps up. The canteen is 2 steps right and 2 steps up. Which is nearer?

learn.reallife: When you walk to a friend's house, you choose the lane with fewer turns and steps. That is choosing the shortest path!

games.title: Shortest path to longest
items: 2 right, 1 up
3 right, 2 up
4 right, 3 up
5 right, 4 up, 1 left

games.title: Which is nearer? Write the steps to the nearer one

quiz.q: A path goes 4 steps right and 3 steps up. How many steps long is it?
quiz.explain: 4 + 3 = 7 steps.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the steps

quiz.q: Path A is 5 steps. Path B is 8 steps. Both reach the well. How many steps shorter is path A?
quiz.explain: 8 − 5 = 3 steps shorter.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two lengths

quiz.q: The park is 2 right and 5 up from home. The shop is 3 right and 3 up. Which is nearer to home?
quiz.explain: Park: 2 + 5 = 7 steps. Shop: 3 + 3 = 6 steps. 6 is less, so the shop is nearer.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the 'right' steps

quiz.q: Rekha goes 3 right, 2 up. Mohan goes to the same place by 3 up, 1 right, 1 down, 2 right. Who walks more steps?
quiz.explain: Rekha: 3 + 2 = 5. Mohan: 3 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 7. Mohan walks more because of his detour.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any path to the same place is the same length

quiz.q: On a grid, the shortest path from the gate to the tap is 4 steps right and 2 steps up. How many steps is the shortest path?
quiz.explain: A path that never goes back is 4 + 2 = 6 steps.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one direction

quiz.q: A path goes 2 right, 1 up, 2 right, 1 up. Another goes 4 right, 2 up. Which is longer?
quiz.explain: First: 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 6. Second: 4 + 2 = 6. They are equal because neither goes backwards.
quiz.mistake: Thinks more turns means a longer path

quiz.q: The swing is 6 steps away. The slide is 9 steps away. How many more steps to the slide than to the swing?
quiz.explain: 9 − 6 = 3 more steps.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Which path is the shortest from start to finish, if finish is 3 right and 3 up?
quiz.explain: 3 + 3 = 6 steps. The other paths go backwards and are longer.
quiz.mistake: Does not count the backward steps

teach.ask: Gappu wants the shortest way to the canteen. How can Gappu decide between two paths?
teach.praise: I counted the steps on both paths and took the one with fewer. I reached the samosas first!
teach.nudge: How do you measure a path, and how do you choose between two?

learn.hook: A drone flies over your school. What does the playground look like from up there?
points: A drone or a bird sees places from directly above. This is a bird's-eye view, or top view.
From above, a round water tank looks like a circle and a building looks like a rectangle roof.
In an aerial picture we can spot buildings by their roof shapes and their places.
A map is a top-view drawing of a place. It shows where things are, using simple shapes and labels.
A map is much smaller than the real place, but things are in the same positions.

example.q: From a drone photo of a school, you see a big empty rectangle with a track around it. What is it most likely?
steps: From above, a playground looks like an open area.
A running track around it is a clue.

learn.reallife: A map app on a phone shows a top view of roads and buildings. Cricket broadcasts use drone cameras to show the whole ground from above.

games.title: What it looks like from above
Maps and top views
items: A map shows a place as seen from above.
Maps are top-view drawings.
A map is the same size as the real place.
A map is much smaller.
On a map, things keep the same positions as in real life.
That is why maps help us find our way.
From a drone, you see the front doors of buildings clearly.
From directly above you mostly see roofs.
A bird's-eye view is another name for a top view.
Both mean looking from directly above.

quiz.q: What do we call a view of a place from directly above?
quiz.explain: Looking from directly above, like a flying bird, gives a bird's-eye (top) view.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up top view and front view

quiz.q: In a drone photo, a round water tank looks like a...
quiz.explain: The top of a round tank is a circle.
quiz.mistake: Imagines the side view instead

quiz.q: What is a map?
options: A top-view drawing that shows where things are
A side view of a building
quiz.explain: A map is a top-view drawing of a place showing where things are.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a map is a front view

quiz.q: In an aerial picture of a school, you see a long rectangle roof next to a big open ground with goal posts. The long roof is most likely...
quiz.explain: A long rectangle roof near the ground is likely a building such as a classroom block.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the shape clues

quiz.q: Why is a map useful?
options: It is bigger than the real place
It shows where places are, so we can find our way
It shows what people are thinking
quiz.explain: A map shows positions of places, which helps us find routes.
quiz.mistake: Thinks maps are only pictures

quiz.q: From above, what can a drone see that a child on the ground cannot?
quiz.explain: From high above, a wall does not block the view of what is behind it.
quiz.mistake: Thinks height does not change what you see

quiz.q: On a school map, the library is drawn to the left of the office. In the real school, where is the library?
options: To the left of the office
To the right of the office
quiz.explain: Maps keep things in the same positions as in real life.
quiz.mistake: Thinks maps flip positions

quiz.q: A cricket ground seen from a helicopter looks like a...
quiz.explain: From above, the cricket ground is a big oval of grass.
quiz.mistake: Imagines the stands from the side

teach.ask: Gappu is flying over the school for the first time! Explain what a bird's-eye view is and how a map is made from it.
teach.praise: So a map is my bird's-eye view drawn small! I can draw my school now!
teach.nudge: From where do you look to make a map, and what does a map show?

topics.title: Routes on a map: the shortest way

learn.hook: From the gate to the library there are three routes. Which one gets you there first?
points: A route is the path you take from one place to another. Trace it with your finger on the map.
There can be several different routes between the same two places.
Count the steps or blocks on each route to compare them.
The shortest route has the fewest steps. It usually avoids going back or going around.
To say which route is longer, compare their total lengths.

example.q: Map: gate to library. Route A: 3 blocks straight then 2 blocks left. Route B: 2 blocks left then 4 blocks straight then 1 block back. Which is shorter?

learn.reallife: Auto drivers and delivery riders choose the shortest route to save time and fuel.

games.title: Shortest route first
items: Route P: 4 blocks
Route Q: 6 blocks
Route R: 7 blocks
Route S: 9 blocks

items.text: The path from one place to another is a ___.
The route with the fewest steps is the ___.
Going back and forth makes a route ___.

quiz.q: Route 1 from home to school is 8 blocks. Route 2 is 11 blocks. Which is shorter and by how much?
quiz.explain: 8 is less than 11, and 11 − 8 = 3.
quiz.mistake: Picks the bigger number as shorter

quiz.q: There are 2 roads from the house to the main road, and 3 roads from the main road to the market. How many different routes are there from the house to the market through the main road?
quiz.explain: Each of the 2 first roads can join any of the 3 next roads: 2 × 3 = 6 routes.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Route A: 4 blocks. Route B: 4 blocks then 2 blocks back then 2 blocks forward. Which is longer?
quiz.explain: Route B is 4 + 2 + 2 = 8 blocks. Route A is only 4.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the back-and-forth steps

quiz.q: Why is a straight route usually the shortest?
options: It does not go back or around
quiz.explain: Going back or around adds extra steps. A straight route avoids that.
quiz.mistake: Thinks wider roads are shorter

quiz.q: To get from the canteen to the gate, Rahul's route is 3 + 2 + 4 blocks. Sana's route is 5 + 3 blocks. Who walks less?
quiz.explain: Rahul: 3 + 2 + 4 = 9. Sana: 5 + 3 = 8. Sana walks less.
quiz.mistake: Compares the number of parts, not the total

quiz.q: A map shows 3 routes from the gate to the hall: 6, 5 and 7 steps. How many steps is the shortest route?
quiz.explain: The smallest of 6, 5 and 7 is 5.
quiz.mistake: Adds all routes

quiz.q: On a map, you trace a route from the gate. What should your finger do?
options: Move along the paths from the start to the end
quiz.explain: Tracing means following the paths step by step from start to end.
quiz.mistake: Jumps across buildings

quiz.q: Route X is 12 steps. Route Y is 3 steps longer than X. How long is route Y?
quiz.explain: 3 steps longer means 12 + 3 = 15.
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding

teach.ask: Gappu wants to go from the gate to the library on the school map. How can Gappu find the shortest route?
teach.praise: I traced all the routes, counted the steps and took the shortest one. Easy!
teach.nudge: How many routes did you look at, and how did you compare them?

topics.title: Giving directions and drawing your own map

learn.hook: 'Go straight, turn left at the big neem tree, and the classroom is on your right.' Could a new student follow your directions?
points: Good directions use words like go straight, turn left, turn right, and stop.
Landmarks help: 'turn right at the water cooler' is easier to follow than 'turn right after 37 steps'.
Left and right depend on which way you are facing. Always say directions as the walker sees them.
To draw your own map, draw the main places as simple shapes in the right positions and label them.
Draw the paths that join the places. Then you can use the map to tell others the way.

example.q: From the gate, Riya goes straight to the office, turns left and walks to the end. The library is on her right. How many turns did she make?
steps: She goes straight first: no turn.
At the end she just looks to her right: no turn needed.

learn.reallife: When a guest calls to ask the way to your home, you give directions with landmarks: 'Turn left after the temple, our house has a blue gate.'

games.title: Steps to draw your own school map
items: Choose the places to show
Draw the gate and main building as shapes
Draw other places in their correct positions
Draw the paths between them
Write labels on each place

games.title: Directions
items: A landmark is an easy-to-spot place, like a big tree or a temple.
Landmarks help people follow directions.
If you turn around, your left becomes your right.
Left and right depend on the way you face.
Good directions say 'go somewhere over there'.
Directions must be clear, like 'go straight, then turn left'.
A map you draw should show places in their correct positions.
Otherwise people will go the wrong way.
A map needs labels so people know what each shape is.
Labels name the places.

quiz.q: Which is the clearest direction for a new student?
options: Go straight, turn right at the water cooler, second door on the left
quiz.explain: It uses clear moves and a landmark.
quiz.mistake: Thinks vague directions are enough

quiz.q: Kiran walks north and turns right. Which direction is he facing now?
quiz.explain: Facing north, your right hand points east. Turning right makes you face east.
quiz.mistake: Turns the wrong way

quiz.q: What is a landmark?
options: An easy-to-spot place used in directions
quiz.explain: A landmark is a place that is easy to see, like a statue or a big tree.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word landmark

quiz.q: Meena is walking towards the school gate. The temple is on her left. She turns around and walks back. Where is the temple now?
quiz.explain: Turning around swaps left and right.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that turning around swaps sides

quiz.q: Sachin draws a map of his school. What must he do so others can use it?
options: Put places in the right positions and label them
quiz.explain: A useful map shows places in their correct positions with labels.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a map is just a drawing

quiz.q: Directions: 'From the gate, go straight 2 blocks, turn left, go 1 block.' How many blocks do you walk?
quiz.explain: 2 + 1 = 3 blocks.
quiz.mistake: Counts the turn as a block

quiz.q: On your map, the office is in front of the gate and the canteen is to the right of the office. A friend at the gate facing the office wants the canteen. What do you say?
options: Go straight to the office, then turn right
Go back out of the gate
quiz.explain: First reach the office by going straight, then the canteen is on the right.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up left and right

quiz.q: Abdul's directions say 'turn left' three times in a row on a square path around a park. After the third left turn, compared to the start, which way does he face?
options: Left of where he started facing
The same way as at the start
The opposite way to the start
Right of where he started facing
quiz.explain: Each left turn is a quarter turn. Three left quarter turns face the same way as one right turn.
quiz.mistake: Thinks three turns bring you back to the start

teach.ask: Gappu is new in school and lost! Tell Gappu how to give and draw directions from the gate to the classroom.
teach.praise: Go straight, turn left at the office, and I can draw it on my map! I will never get lost again.
teach.nudge: Which direction words and landmarks would you use, and what goes on a map?
